Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Practice Plan — Thursday AM, three lanes for one squad of twelve, three lanes, one coach
Resource limits: three lanes, one set of starting blocks, one coach on deck, two and a half hours of pool time.
Everything must be finished by 150 minutes of pool time.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Practice Plan — Thursday AM, three lanes

We have three lanes for two and a half hours and one set of starting blocks. Lane 1 is the sprint group, lane 2 the middle distance, lane 3 the distance group. Everything except the sprint set runs in all three lanes at once; the sprint set runs one lane at a time off the blocks, so lanes wait their turn.

On deck
Brief the squad on the pool deck: what the morning is, who is in which lane, 5 minutes.
Watch the warm-up from the deck and fix anything ugly; 15 minutes.

Warm-up
All three lanes start together: 20 minutes, 800 easy, mixed stroke, breathing every five on the last hundred.

Whiteboard
Call the lanes to the wall when the warm-up is done and walk the main set on the whiteboard; 5 minutes. Nobody pushes off until the board is done.

Kick set
20 minutes of kick, boards for lanes 1 and 2, vertical kick for lane 3, once the whiteboard talk is over.

Main set
Lane 1: 30 to 50 minutes, 40 minutes is the plan.
Lane 2: 30 to 50 minutes, 45 minutes is the plan.
Lane 3: 30 to 50 minutes, 50 minutes is the plan.
Every lane swims its own main set and the sprint set does not start until the last lane is in.

Sprint set
One set of blocks, one lane at a time, 10 minutes each.
Lane 1 goes first, off the blocks, dive starts, 25s flat out.
Lane 2 goes second, same thing, on the lane 1 group's last dive.
Lane 3 goes third and gets the extra rest it will need.
Time the sprints from the deck: 30 minutes, stopwatch and the wall clock.

Cooldown
All three lanes cool down together once the last sprint is in: 10 minutes, 300 easy backstroke and breaststroke.

Debrief
10 minutes on the deck at the end: splits, what to fix, Saturday's meet.

Note
The main set is the only place a lane can run long and the only place the plan gives them room to. Everything after it is a join: the blocks cannot be shared and the cooldown starts together or it does not start at all.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json

  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

This is a Thursday-morning swim practice for one 12-swimmer squad split across three lanes, coached by one on-deck coach, and it must finish within 150 minutes of pool time. The plan is a shared, time-boxed sequence: deck brief, all-lane warm-up, whiteboard explanation gate, kick set, parallel main sets with only the main sets allowing variance, a serialized sprint set using the only starting-blocks setup one lane at a time, a simultaneous cooldown, and a deck debrief. Key constraints are that there are only three lanes, one coach, one set of starting blocks, and a hard 150-minute pool window; sprinting cannot begin until the last lane finishes its main set, cooldown cannot begin until the last sprint lane finishes, and the blocks must be passed from lane to lane in order rather than used simultaneously. The provided source text appears complete for this read-back.

```json
  "servesOrScale": "12 swimmers across 3 lanes, coached by 1 on-deck coach",
  "deadline": "150 minutes from practice start (2 hours 30 minutes of pool time)",
  "constraints": [
    "three swim lanes total",

    "one coach on deck",
    "hard 150-minute pool-time finish",

  ]

```

In Rhylthyme, a **track** is one line of work where steps run one after another, so overlapping activity has to go on a separate track. Each **step** has exactly one duration kind: `fixed` seconds, `variable` min/max/default seconds, or `indefinite` until the person ends it. A **startTrigger** connects a step to the clock or to another step, such as `programStart`, `programStartOffset`, `afterStep`, `afterStepWithBuffer`, `manual`, `onAbort`, or `compound`. `stepId`s must be globally unique across the entire program, not just within one track. Every `task` used by a step needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and that entry’s `maxConcurrent` expresses the real-world limit for a lane, coach, starting blocks, or similar shared resource. Repeated `n` times work should be modeled with `replicates` on one step, using `instances: "each"` and `instances: "all"` for per-instance chaining/barriers, plus `maxInFlight` when an intermediate holding area is smaller than the count.

Expected resource constraints for this workout:

- `swimLane` — `maxConcurrent: 3` — three swim lanes/groups can work at once; 12 swimmers split across 3 lane groups, with 1 coach on deck.
- `startingBlocks` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — only one lane group can use the starting blocks at a time; the sprint set must be serialized.
- `coachDeck` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one coach performs the deck brief, observes warm-up, leads the whiteboard talk, times sprints, and runs the debrief.
- `kickboard` — `maxConcurrent: 2` — if modeled explicitly, only lanes 1 and 2 use kickboards at the same time; lane 3 uses vertical kick.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps; every task needs a resourceConstraint; stepIds are global; repeated work uses replicates with each/all/maxInFlight",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "swimLane", "maxConcurrent": 3 },
    { "task": "startingBlocks", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "coachDeck", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "kickboard", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "actors": 13
}
```

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);
- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.
